## 2. Choose the hook before drawing
Write at least two **short, factual** candidate hooks (three preferred for major campaigns). Each must include **subject, stakes/outcome, speed of comprehension and clarity**; speed means fewer words, not rushed narration.

| Candidate | Exact on-screen text | Spoken first line | First visible subject | Reader reason to watch | Is this claim verified? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | | | | | |
| B | | | | | |
| C | | | | | |

**Selected hook and why:** 

**Three-way alignment test:** Without sound, is the problem understandable from on-screen text and imagery? Without text, do the first visual and spoken words clearly match? Reject a clever-looking opening that contradicts or obscures the actual topic.

**First 5–10 seconds lock-in:** Show the actual problem, a relevant piece of evidence, or a first causal reveal immediately after the hook; do not insert brand/title filler. The hook should make a promise the next beat demonstrably begins to fulfil.

## 3. Native short-form storyboard
Default target 27–35 seconds, vertical 9:16, unless otherwise briefed. Adapt scene timing to explanation; these are planning ranges, not rigid editing cuts. Every shot needs an explanatory reason to exist.

| Beat | Suggested time | Exact on-screen copy | Visual and start → end state | Why the motion helps | Spoken text / silence | Evidence and rights | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Subject + stakes | 0–3s | | | | | | |
| Lock-in proof | 3–9s | | | | | | |
| Mechanism / example A | 9–15s | | | | | | |
| Mechanism / example B | 15–21s | | | | | | |
| Payoff / useful takeaway | 21–27s | | | | | | |
| Real product + CTA | 27–35s | | | | | | |

- One visual continuity lock: approved geometry/reference frame, subject-specific visual vocabulary, camera, palette, typographic hierarchy and crop-safe region:
- Reference videos / permitted inspiration / rights: 
- Explicit negative instructions: no generic icon/slideshow sequences, gratuitous transitions, invented record screenshots, flashing, miniature text or **whooshing/whizzing sounds**.
- Original/reusable vector components and editable animation source:
- Music source / narration source / rights and disclosure:
- Verified CTA **words**, platform-supported link location and actual destination:
- Product reveal must use the real approved cover or real product material, not a synthetic recreation.

## 4. QA on the rendered MP4 — complete before asking for publication
Use [ ] until observed. No box can be checked by inspecting the storyboard alone.

- [ ] Final MP4 exists; identity, duration, frame dimensions, frame rate and codec inspected.
- [ ] Contact-sheet frames sampled at opening, mid-shot, ending and **every scene boundary**.
- [ ] Played the **entire** final render sound-on; timing, motion and subtitles reviewed, not just stills.
- [ ] Phone-size preview checked; hook, headings, small numbers and CTA legible without zoom.
- [ ] All text fits intended boxes and safe zones throughout animations; no clipped words or captions over crucial visuals.
- [ ] Text, voice and the first image communicate the same subject and outcome.
- [ ] The 3–9s beat delivers evidence or meaningful progress rather than delaying the promise.
- [ ] Causal animation, shape changes and camera moves are meaningful, coherent and restrained.
- [ ] Every claimed fact, number, comparison, document and screenshot verified against source.
- [ ] Narration intelligible; transitions clean and quiet; no whoosh/whizz, clipping, abrupt joins or music masking speech.
- [ ] Actual published book cover / real product UI visible, accurate and not obscured.
- [ ] Final CTA and destination tested; no invented Amazon URL, price, review or expected result.
- [ ] Export meets each target platform's current requirements, and any AI disclosure is prepared.
- [ ] Chosen thumbnail and captions inspected; editable source and media provenance retained.

No automatic posting without owner approval. Do not claim publication because a draft or exported file exists.

## 6. Outcome review (after enough data has accumulated)
**Compare matched date ranges and label unavailable data as missing, not zero.** Prefer the same reader problem and product destination for A/B hook comparisons; do not rely on model-based 'virality' forecasts as results.

| Measure | Source and definition | Baseline dates / value | Follow-up dates / value | Caveats |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Impressions | Platform | | | |
| 3s / initial retention (where provided) | Platform | | | |
| Average view duration / completion | Platform | | | |
| Verified attributed website entries | GA4 with consent limitations | | | |
| Product-page visits | GA4 | | | |
| Checkout/link clicks (intent only) | Site/platform | | | |
| Verified orders/refunds | Actual payment/KDP/Etsy record | | | |

**Decision:** improve hook / improve scene 2 / improve landing page / keep / stop / insufficient data. 

**Rule:** viewer attention, outbound clicks, checkout intent and *paid sales* remain distinct, even when a platform reports a convenient combined metric.
